title: Fix the form: labels and a real button
brief:
A form is only useful if people can fill it in. The Drone Society's sign-up form has three problems: the questions are ordinary paragraphs, not labels, so a screen reader does not know which box each question belongs to; the email box is a plain text box; and the big yellow "button" is a div, so you cannot reach it with the Tab key. Fix the form in the HTML box: turn each

question into a

a name for one element on the page, used to connect a label to its box
the attribute that says what kind of box an input is: text, email, checkbox…
the element for a real button; keyboards and screen readers know how to use it, a div is just a box
